parts.note: pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
rate means speed, as in 'at a fast rate'

explanation.surface: A maths lesson about taking a ratio and pairing it with velocity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective (suitable) but is the verb: to take something without permission.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirate is to steal or seize another's work, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: Old and sick need energy tablet

parts.note: past means former or old
ill means sick
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An elderly invalid needs a pill for strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small lozenge or medicated sweet, a kind of tablet.

clue.text: By the way writing on the wall is guidance for travellers

parts.note: a road is a way
the writing on the wall is a sign or portent

explanation.surface: Incidentally, graffiti offers directions to tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like the idiom 'incidentally'; 'By' is a link and 'the way' gives ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A road sign shows drivers directions, distances and warnings.

parts.note: to tote is to carry
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Tribal emblems bear inscriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Totems are objects or animals revered as emblems of a clan.

clue.text: Turn away unfamiliar blend of tea

parts.note: alien means strange or unfamiliar

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters of the word tea are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a strange new mix of tea leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blend of' rearranges TEA into ATE, which follows ALIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to estrange them, making them turn away.

explanation.surface: Top position for an aviator.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the lead is to be in front; to lead is also to guide or steer, as a pilot does.

clue.text: Long story about the same plague

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the long story goes around the other piece

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem or tale
idem is Latin for 'the same'

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale retelling the same pestilence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EPIC around IDEM, the Latin used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of disease, as a plague is.

clue.text: Summon up a device containing oxygen

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the trick wraps round the chemical symbol

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or device
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Conjuring up an apparatus that holds gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'device' looks like a gadget but means a trick; 'containing' puts O inside RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse feelings is to stir or evoke them, to call them forth.

explanation.surface: An animal keeps on living.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to tolerate hardship, and also to last or survive.

clue.text: Will not need yard behind hut

indicators.note: the yard abbreviation is placed behind, i.e. after, the other piece

parts.note: shan't is the contraction of shall not, i.e. will not

explanation.surface: Someone declares they won't require any garden space at the back of their cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text reads 'but'; the printed page has 'hut', the definition. 'behind' puts Y after SHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a crude shack or cabin, a kind of hut.

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or blight
I is the Roman numeral one
gold is a yellow colour

explanation.surface: A plant disease attacking a single yellow bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' does two duties in the surface but the definition is the whole phrase 'yellow flower'; GOLD comes from 'yellow' within the wordplay reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The marigold is a garden plant with bright orange or golden blooms.

clue.text: Huge bird caught in a revolving vessel

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: revolving turns round, so this run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An enormous bird is trapped inside a spinning container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' turns C IN A into ANIC after TIT; 'vessel' nods to the ship Titanic.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, after the giant Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Strangely, no man is island, leading to sleep problem

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island on maps

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are arranged in an odd, unusual order

explanation.surface: A twist on Donne's 'no man is an island', leading to a sleepless night.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on John Donne's line 'No man is an island'; the letters NOMANIS plus I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is chronic inability to fall or stay asleep.

explanation.surface: A Roman statesman's flag gets trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banner' is not a flag but one who bans: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor and banned luxuries.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor removes objectionable material from a text; Cato held the Roman magistracy that policed public morals.

parts.note: a sports pitch is a ground

explanation.surface: A playing field stranded on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' suggests a drink with ice, but here means stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has run aground is stuck on rocks or shallows.

clue.text: Make a note of old firm's trademark

parts.note: to log something is to record or note it

explanation.surface: Jotting down an ancient company's brand mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is the emblem or symbol a company uses as its brand.

clue.text: Legal practitioners make a great deal

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
to make money is to gain it

explanation.surface: Lawyers strike a profitable agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a great deal' looks like 'a lot', but means a good purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is a purchase at an unusually good price.

clue.text: Get in touch with residents' leader in Deal

indicators.note: the leading letter of residents is put in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: to contact someone is to get in touch with them

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Contact the head of the tenants' group in the Kent town of Deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a coastal town in Kent, but here it is the definition: an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a formal agreement between parties.

clue.text: Behave less tamely and cause utter confusion

explanation.surface: Run riot and baffle everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the word: BE WILDER, behave in a less tame way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wilder is acting more untamed; to bewilder is to perplex completely.

parts.note: a bright future is a promising one
a show that is on is being shown

explanation.surface: A hopeful display somewhere in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county on England's south coast; the definition is a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a seaside city on the Sussex coast.

clue.text: Keep an eye on classroom helper

explanation.surface: Supervising a pupil who assists the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor is to watch over; in schools a monitor is a pupil given duties such as handing out books.

explanation.surface: Tolerating a game you dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is not a game but the verb, as in to sport a hat; 'put up with' is the British sense of wear = tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who won't wear an idea won't tolerate it, and to sport clothing is to have it on.

explanation.surface: Itemising the facts with cool aloofness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detachment' is not aloofness but a small military unit sent off on a task.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail is to itemise fully; a detail is also a squad assigned to a duty.

indicators.note: about means around, so the face surrounds the wrongdoing

parts.note: mug is slang for face
sin is evil or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Contemplating a wicked expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but puts MUG around SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Musing is pondering or reflecting quietly.

indicators.note: scattered means strewn about, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: Weapons lying strewn across a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the weapons also describes them once strewn thinly about.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly spread, as weapons scattered across a field would be.

indicators.note: read as 'in an original way', the word quite is given a new, inventive arrangement

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic letters for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A sporting principle that, at first, was quite obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like it asks for a first letter, but here it rearranges QUITE into EQUIT; Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is fairness and impartiality, giving each side even-handed treatment.

parts.note: a snap is a sharp cracking noise
a ping is a short high ringing noise

explanation.surface: Two bangs heard: perhaps someone is firing a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns, but snapping is taking photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking snaps with a camera is photography, also called shooting pictures.

explanation.surface: Sad plumage drawn on a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on paper' nods to where the clue sits: in the Down list of the printed puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is being sad; the soft fine plumage of birds used in pillows has the same name.

clue.text: Disney artist makes changes to airman

indicators.note: making changes to the letters of the phrase to airman puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A cartoonist redraws a pilot character.
explanation.definitionFit: An animator draws the frames of cartoons such as those made by the Disney studio.

explanation.surface: A check mark on the page signals that the work passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' is the British colloquial word for buying on credit ('on tick'), not only a check mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying on tick means buying on deferred payment; giving someone recognition or praise is giving them that same word.

explanation.surface: Signal lights along an airstrip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing' is not a runway but the act of alighting, as when a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To light on something is to settle on it, and flares are a form of illumination.

clue.text: He starts north to organise enclosure for birds

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of the word north gives its opening letter

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it

explanation.surface: A man heads north to set up a chicken coop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen-run is the fenced yard where chickens are kept.
